Winner: We Need Diverse Books The 2025 Innovator’s Award winner is We Need Diverse Books (WNDB), a nonprofit organization dedicated to increasing diversity and inclusion in publishing. What began in 2014 as a trending hashtag on social media, has expanded into organized mentorships, workshops, grants and professional development programs. WNDB supports writers, illustrators and publishing professionals to ensure better representation on the bookshelves, and also works closely with educators and libraries to drive systemic change across the publishing ecosystem. Matthews ────────────── ROBERT KIRSCH AWARD ────────────── The Robert Kirsch Award recognizes the body of work of a living author who resides in and/or whose work focuses on the West and whose contributions to American letters deserve special recognition. Winner: Amy Tan Acclaimed author Amy Tan is 2025’s Robert Kirsch Award winner which recognizes a writer with a substantial connection to the American West. Her expansive work, including “The Joy Luck Club,” “The Kitchen God’s Wife” and “The Bonesetter’s Daughter,” explores the immigrant experience and family bonds. Born in Oakland to immigrant parents, Tan gives voice to the Chinese American experience and the American story. In “The Backyard Bird Chronicles,” she turns her observational eye to nature, chronicling her foray into birding through daily entries and sketches. Her accolades, including the National Humanities Medal and the 2026 Preston Award, solidify her legacy as a titan of literary excellence and cultural impact. ──────────────────────── SCI-FI, FANTASY & SPECULATIVE FICTION ──────────────────────── Winner: Luminous: A Novel , Silvia Park, Simon & Schuster Finalists:

Winner: Amanda Gorman The 2024 Innovator’s Award winner is Amanda Gorman, the award-winning writer and activist, and the youngest inaugural poet in U.S. history. Gorman has used her platform to raise awareness on a host of issues from climate change and social justice to literacy.
